messages.content: What is the acceleration a ball will reach if it's thrown straight upwards with a velocity of 5 m/s?

function.name: calculate_maximum_height
function.description: Calculate the maximum height an object will reach if it's thrown straight upwards with an initial velocity, ignoring air resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

initial_velocity.description: The initial velocity in meters per second. This is a float type value.

gravity.description: The acceleration due to gravity in meters per second squared, default value is 9.8. This is a float type value.

message.content:
When you throw a ball straight upward (ignoring air resistance), the only acceleration acting on it is gravity.  
That acceleration is constant and points downward, so the ball’s acceleration is

\[
a = -\,g \approx -9.8\ \text{m/s}^2
\]

(The negative sign indicates the direction is opposite to the upward motion.)
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What is the acceleration a ball will reach if it's thrown straight upwards with a velocity of 5 m/s?" They likely want the acceleration due to gravity, which is constant -9.8 m/s^2 downward. But maybe they want to compute maximum height? The question: "What is the acceleration a ball will reach if it's thrown straight upwards with a velocity of 5 m/s?" That phrasing is odd: acceleration a ball will reach? Actually acceleration is constant. So answer: -9.8 m/s^2 (downwards). Could also mention ignoring air resistance. So answer: -9.8 m/s^2. No need to call function.
